## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical search (e.g. BM25) with dense vector search, then merges the two ranked result sets to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity.

### Merge Strategy: Reciprocal Rank Fusion

A common approach to merging results from multiple retrieval methods is **reciprocal rank fusion (RRF)**. This technique ranks items by the reciprocal of their position in each result set, allowing fair comparison across different retrieval mechanisms that may have different scoring scales.

### Performance Profile

Hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms either method alone on queries mixing rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs) with natural language intent. This makes it the default retrieval pattern in production RAG systems, where queries are often heterogeneous and require both precision (lexical matching) and semantic understanding.
